{{Quote|Smugglers establish inconsistencies so that if they're caught carrying contraband, they can claim the luggage belongs to someone else.|Immigration Inspector Modt|<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>}}
The '''Coruscanti Immigration Service''', also known as '''Customs and Immigration''', was the customs and immigration [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|enforcement service]] for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. The agency was charged with verifying the identity of persons wanting to enter Coruscant and they monitored for suspected [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]] operations. They also tracked the levels of immigration and residency of various groups and [[Species/Legends|species]] on Coruscant.

During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] between the Galactic Alliance and the [[Confederation]], the immigration service assisted the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] and the Alliance secret police, the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]], by monitoring for suspected [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorists]] entering Coruscant. They also provided information on the numbers of species living on Coruscant who may have had ties with the Confederation or were sympathetic to its cause.

At the start of the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Lost Tribe of Sith emergence)|Liberation of Coruscant]] by the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] from the control of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], the Lost Tribe had placed some of its members within the immigration service, unknown to the service's regular [[Officer/Legends|officers]] and [[Inspector/Legends|inspectors]], to identify and capture any [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] attempting to enter Coruscant. However, their efforts were fruitless and the Jedi were able to infiltrate and reclaim Coruscant.

==Overview==
{{Quote|Best intelligence is that Customs and Immigration got a tip-off about three Corellian agents and a bounty hunter they made contact with, and CSF tracked them down here.|GAG Captain Lon Shevu|<ref name="Bloodlines" />}}
The Coruscanti Immigration Service, also called Customs and Immigration, was an immigration and customs [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|enforcement service]] for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] under the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. It was responsible for verifying the identity of all persons entering Coruscant and ensuring their paperwork was in order, monitoring for [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]],<ref name="Apocalypse" /> [[Spy/Legends|spies]], [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorists]], and others attempting to enter Coruscant illegally,<ref name="Bloodlines" /> searching incoming vessels and check their passengers and manifests, operating customs checkpoints at Coruscant's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]],<ref name="Apocalypse" /> and tracking the immigration, emigration, and residency population levels of groups and [[Species/Legends|species]] on Coruscant.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

Immigration [[Inspector/Legends|inspectors]] and their supervising [[Officer/Legends|officers]], such as [[Captain/Legends|captains]], were supported at spaceport checkpoints by [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] from [[Galactic Alliance Security]] (GAS). The GAS troopers would provide extra manpower for searches and to make arrests should the inspectors need it. Immigration captains also had the authority to order GAS troopers to hold suspects for further investigation.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Any information that the immigration service received on suspected smugglers or other wanted persons who made it past checkpoints, was turned over the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] (CSF) which would then track the suspects through Coruscant's [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] and make an arrest if possible.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

==History==
{{Quote|You're lying. And I want to know why. Shall we have a look inside those traveling cases you're carrying?|Immigration Captain Suhale|<ref name="Apocalypse" />}}
In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] between the Galactic Alliance and the [[Confederation]], [[Corellian/Legends|Corellians]] were closely monitored as suspected [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorists]]. The immigration service estimated that over twenty million Corellians lived on Coruscant. The number of Corellians caused concern for Galactic Alliance [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] who had ordered the newly formed counter terrorism police force, the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]] (GAG), to begin interning Corellians. It was at that time that the immigration service received a tip about three suspected Corellian agents and a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] who had slipped past their checkpoints. The immigration service turned the information over to the CSF which was able to track the four suspects. The information was then given to the GAG who arrested the suspects.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

In [[44 ABY]] the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] had managed to infiltrate Coruscant and had secretly taken over the Galactic Alliance [[Office of the Chief of State|government]] and [[Galactic Alliance Senate|Senate]] as well as many of the planet's vital [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucracies]]. Subsequently, the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] under [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] planned to enter and [[Liberation of Coruscant (Lost Tribe of Sith emergence)|liberate]] the planet. [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] operatives and been planted within the immigration service to monitor for [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] attempting to enter Coruscant. [[Unidentified Sith immigration inspector|One]] Sith in particular posed as a corrupt inspector who took bribes while checking incoming ships. He inspected the passengers of the [[Passenger liner/Legends|starliner]] ''[[Plain Lady]]'' and cross-examined the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] siblings [[Valin Horn|Valin]] and [[Jysella Horn]], who at the time were disguised. Detecting no falsehood from the sibling's answers through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Sith inspector allowed them to go their way.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

Meanwhile at the [[Galactic Center Spaceport]], Jedi Knights [[Yaqeel Saav'etu]] and [[Yantahar Bwua'tu]], while being questioned by immigration Inspector [[Modt]], had aroused suspicion in the Force by immigration Captain [[Suhale]], who was reality a Sith. Jedi [[Bazel Warv]], seeing the two knights were being questioned by the Sith, was able to find some [[Spice/Legends|spice]] smugglers and convinced them to give him their illegal packages. He then intentionally aroused the suspicion of Suhale who ordered him over the inspection station. Suhale proceeded to question him and ordered that he open the packages and suitcases, believing she had caught several Jedi. However, Inspector Modt, unaware of the maneuvering going on the Force, assumed that in reality the three simply had some form of contraband and showed disdain for his superior's obvious inexperience with dealing with smugglers. When the cases were opened, revealing the [[Neutron Pixie]] spice, Modt's assumptions appeared to have been accurate. Suhale, believing the spice to be the reason the three suspected Jedi had been uncomfortable in the Force, ordered them arrested by a GA Security squad. Promising to personally submit it as evidence, Suhale took possession of the high valued spiced, much to the disapproval of Inspector Modt.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Coruscanti Immigration Service was first mentioned in ''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]'', written by [[Karen Traviss]] and published on [[August 29]], [[2006]]. It later appeared ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]'', written by [[Troy Denning]] and pusblished on [[March 13]], [[2012]]
